title: I made an RPG where the NPCs don't have to agree with your party's terrible plan
author: tschilpi
selftext:
Gather some companions, head into the frontier, negotiate with hobgoblins, get caught in a rivalry—or start a fight and try talking your way out afterwards.



I'm building Lore & Legends Maker to capture that part of a D&D session where the party comes up with something the adventure didn't plan for. NPCs have their own motivations, companions have opinions, and things don't have to go your way.



I've been working on this solo for three years. This is gameplay from the latest patch.



How I'm using AI: Claude helps turn world notes into NPCs, factions, encounters and adventures. Claude Code and Codex help implement the game systems, and I let Claude play through adventures to help find problems. During play, AI interprets player actions and handles NPC dialogue.



The lesson that helped most was keeping world state separate from narration: the game stores what changed, and the AI describes the result. That gives later interactions actual consequences to work from.



What would you try with this party that a normal dialogue menu wouldn't let you do?
